mechanism_narrative: The persistent and accelerating decline in retail and recreation mobility over the past four weeks indicates a strong underlying trend of reduced non-essential activity that will continue to drive RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, or shows a sustained increase for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in transit station activity below -75% from baseline signifies an intensification of mobility restrictions or public adherence, which will directly translate to a continued suppression of non-essential retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite TRANSIT falling below -75% from baseline, or TRANSIT does not fall below -75%.

mechanism_narrative: The observed inverse relationship where increasing time spent at home (RESIDENTIAL) directly correlates with decreasing retail and recreation visits (RETAIL_REC) will persist, driving RETAIL_REC further down as people continue to prioritize staying home over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL continues to rise, or RESIDENTIAL begins to decline while RETAIL_REC also declines.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained and deep decline in WORKPLACES mobility reflects widespread work-from-home policies and business closures, which will continue to remove a primary driver of weekday retail footfall, leading to further suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows a significant increase despite WORKPLACES remaining below -50% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in PARKS mobility, indicated by two consecutive weeks of increase, suggests a growing public desire for outdoor leisure, which could spill over into local, open-air retail and recreation, leading to a modest rebound in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or remains flat over the next 14 days, even if PARKS mobility increases for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The ongoing decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, even for essential services, indicates a heightened level of public caution and adherence to stay-at-home orders, which will inevitably keep non-essential RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows an increase over the next 7 days despite GROCERY_PHARM continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of severely reduced public transit usage and a significant drop in workplace attendance creates a strong negative feedback loop, making it less convenient and less necessary for people to visit retail and recreation venues, thus further suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -70% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: An early signal of impending policy easing, indicated by any week-on-week increase in either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, will trigger anticipatory behavioral changes, leading to a modest positive shift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as people prepare for a return to activity.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT shows any week-on-week increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or remains flat over the next 28 days, despite a week-on-week increase in either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT mobility.
